items.title: DPSP — Nature, Source & Article 37
items.body:
The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are guidelines in **Part IV (Articles 36-51)** directing the State to establish a **social welfare state** securing social, economic and political justice. They were **borrowed from the Irish Constitution** (which took the idea from Spain) and embody the **Objectives Resolution** ideals.

Under **Article 37**, DPSP are **non-justiciable** — not enforceable by any court — yet **'fundamental in the governance of the country'**, and it is the duty of the State to apply them in making laws. They resemble the **'Instrument of Instructions'** issued to the Governor-General under the **Government of India Act, 1935**. Courts may use them as an **interpretive tool** to test the reasonableness of a law, and their real sanction is **political/moral** — accountability at the ballot box.
keyPoints: DPSP are in Part IV, Articles 36-51, borrowed from the Irish Constitution (originally Spain).
Article 37 — DPSP are non-justiciable but fundamental in governance; duty of State to apply them.
They resemble the 'Instrument of Instructions' under the Government of India Act, 1935.
Aim: shift from a police state to a welfare state; economic democracy alongside political democracy.
Sanction is political/moral, not legal; courts use DPSP to judge a law's reasonableness.

items.title: Threefold Classification of DPSP
items.body:
Though the Constitution does not classify them, DPSP are conventionally grouped into three categories:

| Category | Basis | Key Articles |
|---|---|---|
| **Socialistic** | social & economic justice | 38 (justice, reduce inequality), 39 (livelihood, wealth distribution, equal pay), 39A (legal aid), 41 (work, education, public assistance), 42 (maternity relief), 43 (living wage), 43A (worker participation), 47 (nutrition & health) |
| **Gandhian** | Gandhi's ideals | 40 (village panchayats), 43 (cottage industries), 46 (SC/ST & weaker sections), 47 (prohibition), 48 (cattle/cow slaughter) |
| **Liberal-Intellectual** | liberalism & science | 44 (Uniform Civil Code), 45 (early childhood care), 48 (modern agriculture), 48A (environment), 49 (monuments), 50 (judiciary-executive separation), 51 (international peace) |

Note that some articles (e.g. **47, 48, 43**) straddle categories.
keyPoints: Socialistic: Art 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A, 47 — economic justice & equality.
Gandhian: Art 40, 43, 46, 47, 48 — panchayats, cottage industries, prohibition, cattle.
Liberal-Intellectual: Art 44, 45, 48, 48A, 49, 50, 51.
Article 39: livelihood, prevention of concentration of wealth, equal pay for equal work.
Article 44 = UCC; Article 50 = separation of judiciary from executive; Article 51 = international peace.

items.title: New Directive Principles Added by Amendments
items.body:
Later amendments enriched Part IV with new directives:

| Amendment | Addition |
|---|---|
| **42nd (1976)** | **Art 39A** (equal justice & free legal aid), **Art 43A** (worker participation in management), **Art 48A** (protection of environment, forests & wildlife) |
| **86th (2002)** | Recast **Art 45** to early childhood care & education (below 6 yrs); made free education for 6-14 a Fundamental Right under **Art 21A** |
| **97th (2011)** | **Art 43B** — promotion of voluntary formation, autonomous functioning and democratic control of **cooperative societies** |

There are also **directives outside Part IV**: **Art 335** (SC/ST claims to services), **Art 350A** (mother-tongue instruction at primary stage) and **Art 351** (development of the Hindi language).
keyPoints: 42nd Amendment (1976) added Art 39A, 43A and 48A.
86th Amendment (2002) recast Art 45 (early childhood care) and made education a FR via Art 21A.
97th Amendment (2011) added Art 43B on cooperative societies.
Directives outside Part IV: Art 335 (SC/ST services), Art 350A (mother tongue), Art 351 (Hindi).

items.title: Fundamental Rights vs DPSP — Evolution of Balance
items.body:
The relationship between Fundamental Rights (FR) and DPSP evolved through landmark cases:

| Case | Year | Holding |
|---|---|---|
| **Champakam Dorairajan** | 1951 | FR prevail over DPSP in conflict → led to 1st, 4th, 17th Amendments |
| **Golaknath** | 1967 | FR are 'sacrosanct' and cannot be amended to implement DPSP → prompted 24th & 25th Amendments |
| **Kesavananda Bharati** | 1973 | DPSP cannot override the **basic structure**; recognised the FR-DPSP balance |
| **Minerva Mills** | 1980 | Absolute primacy of DPSP over Art 14 & 19 would destroy the balance, which is itself part of the basic structure |

**Article 31C** (25th Amendment, 1971) protects laws implementing **Art 39(b)/(c)** from challenge under Art 14 and 19. The goal is **harmony** — FR and DPSP are complementary, not adversarial.
keyPoints: Champakam Dorairajan (1951): FR prevail over DPSP → led to the 1st Amendment.
Golaknath (1967): FR cannot be amended to enforce DPSP → led to 24th & 25th Amendments.
Kesavananda Bharati (1973): DPSP cannot override the basic structure.
Minerva Mills (1980): the FR-DPSP balance is part of the basic structure.
Article 31C shields laws implementing Art 39(b)/(c) from Art 14 and 19.

items.title: Implementation, Utility & Criticism
items.body:
**Implementation** — Key measures giving effect to DPSP: **land reform / zamindari abolition** (Art 39), **Minimum Wages Act 1948** and **Equal Remuneration Act 1976** (Art 39, 43), **nationalisation of banks & insurance**, **Panchayati Raj via the 73rd Amendment 1992** (Art 40), **MGNREGA 2005** (Art 41 right to work), protection of monuments and wildlife, and **NITI Aayog (2015)** replacing the Planning Commission for balanced development.

**Utility** — a yardstick for government performance; a framework for future legislation; ensures social justice and sustainable development.

**Criticism** — no legal force (non-justiciable); illogically arranged with no clear priority; can create Centre-State tension over implementation; conservative political philosophy in parts.
keyPoints: Land reforms, Minimum Wages Act (1948) and Equal Remuneration Act (1976) implement Art 39/43.
MGNREGA (2005) advances Art 41 (right to work); 73rd Amendment (1992) implements Art 40.
NITI Aayog (2015) replaced the Planning Commission for balanced development.
Utility: yardstick for government performance and a framework for legislation.
Criticism: no legal force, illogical arrangement, possible Centre-State tension.

items.title: For Mains — Directive Principles of State Policy
items.body:
## Why Mains asks this (Paper-III, Polity & Governance; clauses M3-1, M3-15a)

DPSP answers reward the **FR-DPSP balance, the welfare-state argument, and implementation-vs-criticism**, not article-listing.

| Dimension | What to deploy |
|---|---|
| **Nature** | Non-justiciable (Art 37) but 'fundamental in governance'; 'Instrument of Instructions' (GoI Act 1935) |
| **Classification** | Socialistic (38, 39, 41, 43, 47), Gandhian (40, 43, 46, 47, 48), Liberal-Intellectual (44, 45, 48A, 50, 51) |
| **FR-DPSP balance** | Champakam (1951) → Golaknath (1967) → Kesavananda (1973) → Minerva Mills (1980, balance = basic structure) |
| **Implementation** | Land reforms, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Equal Remuneration Act 1976, MGNREGA 2005, 73rd/74th Amdts, RTE 2009 |
| **Criticism** | No legal force, illogically arranged, no priority, Centre-State friction, conservative in parts |
| **Way forward** | Make key directives justiciable incrementally (as with RTE → Art 21A); outcome budgeting; SDG alignment |

**Data / authorities to quote:** Granville Austin called FR and DPSP the Constitution's 'conscience'; Minerva Mills (1980) 'harmony and balance'; Art 31C (25th Amendment, 1971); Uttarakhand UCC (in force 27 Jan 2025) as a live Art 44 instance; MGNREGA (Art 41); NITI Aayog (2015) and SDG localisation as modern welfare-state tools.

**AP angle:** AP operationalises DPSP through mandal-level Panchayati Raj (Art 40), welfare and nutrition schemes (Art 47 — e.g. midday meals, PDS), women-focused SHG/DWCRA programmes (Art 39/46), and legal-aid machinery (Art 39A); the state's heavy welfare-scheme orientation after bifurcation is a textbook DPSP illustration.

**Use in answers:** frame DPSP and FR as 'two wheels of the chariot of justice'; use the four-case ladder for the balance question; pair each classification with one concrete scheme to show application; close with 'the UCC and RTE show directives maturing into enforceable rights'. A three-circle classification diagram adds structure.
keyPoints: Argue the welfare state via Art 37 and the Socialistic/Gandhian/Liberal classification with concrete schemes.
Use Champakam → Golaknath → Kesavananda → Minerva Mills for the FR-DPSP balance (basic structure).
Quote Granville Austin's 'conscience of the Constitution' and Minerva Mills' 'harmony and balance'.
Cite implementation: land reforms, wage laws, MGNREGA (Art 41), 73rd/74th Amdts (Art 40), RTE 2009.
Use Uttarakhand UCC (in force Jan 2025) as a live Article 44 example; note DPSP maturing into rights.
AP angle: mandal Panchayati Raj, welfare/nutrition schemes, SHG/DWCRA, legal aid as DPSP in practice.
items.source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity (DPSP); Granville Austin; Minerva Mills (1980); Constitution of India Part IV
